IELTS Writing Task 1: Bar Charts and Tables

By the end of this exercise, you can compare figures in a bar chart or table, group what is similar and write an overview.

About this task in the exam

In IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 you describe one or more graphs, charts or tables, or a diagram, in at least 150 words. The whole Writing test lasts 60 minutes, and about 20 of them are usually spent on Task 1. Task 2 counts twice as much, so do not spend longer than that. Bar charts and tables often show no change over time. Then your job is to compare: find the biggest and smallest figures, group the ones that are similar, and sum up the main differences in an overview.

📖
Ex A – Model answerComplete a model report on a bar chart with comparison phrases that fit the data
🔢
Ex B – Proportions8 items: turn figures into words, such as just over a quarter
🔭
Ex C – The overview6 items: choose the sentence that sums up the main features
✍️

Exercise A

A model report

Study the bar chart and the table, then choose the word or phrase that matches the data for each gap.

Before you start — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
The task

The bar chart below shows how students in four countries travel to university. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. (Invented practice data.)

How students travel to university (% of students), Countries A–D
ModeABCD
Car (solid)48123024
Public transport (striped)30264536
Bicycle (dotted)644912
Walking (white)16181628
Model report

The bar chart compares how students in four countries travel to university, shown as a percentage of all students in each country.

Overall, the car was the most common way to travel in Country A, bicycles were the first choice in Country B. Public transport was popular everywhere and accounted for the highest proportion of journeys in both Country C and Country D.

Almost half of the students in Country A (48%) drove, and the share of car users there was that in Country B, where the figure was only 12%. In Country C, public transport was used by of students (45%), and Country B had of cyclists of the four countries, at 44%.

Only 6% of students in Country A cycled, 44% in Country B. Walking was most common in Country D, where of students (28%) went on foot, while Countries A and C had of walkers, at 16%. Finally, car use in Country C (30%) was in Country D (24%).

Exercise C

The overview

A Task 1 report needs an overview: one or two sentences with the main features and no detailed figures. For each chart or table, choose the best overview sentence. Items 5 and 6 review the Describing Trends exercise.

Exercise D

Write your own Task 1 report

The table below shows the percentage of household spending that went on housing, food and transport in four countries in one year. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. (Invented practice data.)

The data
Household spending by category (% of total spending)
CategoryPQRS
Housing35223025
Food15282012
Transport12101820

P, Q, R and S are four countries.

Your report
Introduction (paraphrase the task) → overview (the main features, no detailed figures) → two paragraphs that group similar figures and compare them. You do not need to mention every number. In the exam you would have about 20 minutes; here there is no time limit.
